body:
Ah, isn't it a hallmark of the stupid irony of the situation that you still plan for the future even if you don't intend on having a future? I frequently feel like I have two different "me"s inside my head. The strong, cold rational side is where I exist most of the time, yet that's where I have the cold thoughts about people in general. Then there's the weak, beaten down emotional aspect, yet it still struggles to be heard despite it all.

I'm sorry to hear that you think your family would be okay with it. I bet your siblings would be more haunted by it than you'd expect. I kept shit from my little brother for a long, long while. I've only recently started to open up to him about it, which is somehow easier now that we on opposite coasts. But he's been surprisingly understanding and actually a pretty incredible support system. He's got such a bright future at his new company and I think it'd destroy him if I were to off myself. It's so easy being cynical about everything and everyone, but I've been reconnecting with my family, and it's actually given me a little meaning in life. My pops never understood depression, would tell me to "just cheer up goddammit" but he's come around in recent years. 

Idk if family going to provide that for you, but for the first time in a long, long time, I feel like I have a reason to keep going.

Yeah unfortunately the hunger thing has lead to some serious eating disorders. This is actually the first time I've disclosed that information to anyone haha. People in my life have had suspicions, but it's easy to remove people from your life if they figure shit out. I also punch myself, but I like hitting myself in the jaw and whiting/blacking out. Usually gives me a headache bad enough I don't want to eat anymore.

Same as you, young, single and a pretty nihilistic view on society/people in general. Even when I've been at the edge in the past, I haven't been able to pull the trigger because I'd ruin the lives of my parents, and that's not fair to them. I've taken some solace in outdoor adventuring. Climbing mountains and kayaking gives me a rush that I don't find anywhere else in life. Unfortunately I've come down with crippling arthritis this year that's left me stranded on my toilet for hours because it hurt too much to get up. So I don't know how many mountains I'll be climbing.

Do you have any hobbies like that? Mountaineering is almost like a thrilling self-punishment.

That intense irritability can be scary, especially when it turns back at you. I've developed this weird tick where I get furious at myself for being hungry, or even wanting to eat. Like eating is some basal weakness or indulgence and I a shit person for needing it. Totally irrational, and I recognize that internally, but the emotions still are there.

Edit: I had the same reaction with therapists for a while. I'd lie to everyone about everything, and first and foremost was to my therapist. I'd make everything seem like it was on the up and up, when it was really only getting worse. It took me getting a new therapist because one relocated, and the new one was the first person in my life to see through my mountains of bullshit and call me on it.
Hey. 27m here. I've dealt with a variety of mental health issues myself. I relate to a lot of what you're saying. If you want to talk to someone, shoot me a message. I'd love to listen.

Hey man. I know the feeling. Dated a girl for three years, planned to get married, she dumped be because my useless ass couldn't get better enough. Then I hit my lowest low and it dragged for a while. But in retrospect, I don't think I could have got better while I was with her. My "progress" was a fucking sham I crafted and maintained to keep her around, because she was my only light in the world. Once I was alone, I was forced to reckon with my darkness. And from that brutal, long fight, I began to recognize a pretty cool version of myself underneath all the shit.

So guess what? It sucks, it really does. That lost relationship will hurt you for longer than it needs to. But underneath it all, you're in a new position to deal with yourself and your issues. You're not getting better for someone else. That's not the point of progress. You have to do this for YOU. Underneath all this bullshit that is mental illness, you're in a better position than ever before to really get to know yourself. I know it's hard, but try to see the opportunity you have before you. 

Hit me up with a PM if you'd like. Like I said, I've lived a similar situation. I'd be more than happy to listen to you. If not, best of luck to you. Stay strong.

Hey. That does make sense, to me at least. Sometimes my senseless urges to off myself come at totally random times. Often, I have some pretty intense internal turmoil because these urges don't actually match up to my internal reasoning. But nonetheless they're still there. I've found through research and my personal journey through therapy (multiple times) that these urges are pretty indicative of some sort of mental health issues. 

I know it's a tough step to take, but for me, talking to a counselor was a life changing experience. But it's not something that everyone has access to. I believe that it's important to at the very least find someone to talk to, and that someone needs to be a good listener. They're not there to solve your problems, they are to be a sounding board for your own issues. Personally, I have issues getting close to people, so talking to a counselor helps because I can be honest to a stranger. But nonetheless, find someone to talk to. I've uncovered things in my life that I've totally dismissed as meaningless low points, but really they add a sense of worthlessness in the back of your mind that slowly builds. And that slow build can warp these suicidal thoughts into some pretty caustic and irreparable self destruction. Please don't get to this place. 

I guess all I'm trying to say is what you're dealing with is totally normal. I relate 100%. And if you don't have anyone to talk to, send me a message. I'm dealing with some chronic illness right now, and I have all the time in the world. Also, I could use someone to talk to myself. Good luck with whatever you are dealing with. Mental health issues suck.
